THE CAT ON THE BASKETS: a small cat asleep on a tilting pile of woven baskets aboard a bobbing skiff, one ear twitching, plainly unbothered by the entire clattering market around it
THE ROOFTOP CAT: a small cat sitting upright on a painted cabin roof, side-on, watching the water below with the focused patience of someone who has already decided they own this canal
THE LEDGE CAT: a cat stretched full-length along a warm tiled ledge above the water, tiny in the frame, its tail hanging over the edge and swaying very slightly with the current of passing boats
THE REACHING CAT: a small cat crouched at a gunwale with one amber paw dipped toward the water, watching a flicker of silver just below the surface with total and alarming concentration
THE SECOND ROOFTOP CAT: a small cat wedged between two clay roof tiles high above the stalls, side-on and tiny in the frame, sitting in a precise square of warm light as though it reserved the spot
THE DOG-SIZED CARP: three carp the size of dogs nosing slowly between the hulls at mid-distance, their broad orange shapes perfectly legible through the flat green water, moving like slow embers
THE TURNING FISH: a pale fish shape the length of an oar turning in a long lazy spiral beneath a moored boat, its white belly catching what little light reaches the shadowed hull
THE SILVER SCATTER: a bright loose cloud of tiny silver shapes below the surface under a stall's overhang, flickering all at once in the same direction as though sharing a single sudden thought
THE SPOTTED CARP: one large spotted carp holding perfectly still in the deep shadow of a hull, its gold and black pattern vivid even in the dim green water, the only motionless thing in the canal
THE DEEP ORANGE PAIR: two fat carp at mid-distance pressing their broad faces up toward a gap between hulls, their orange backs glowing beneath the surface like coals seen through green glass
THE DUCK CROSSING: a neat line of small ducks crossing the open water between the stalls, tiny in the frame, each one trailing a thin bright ripple, proceeding with unhurried official dignity

THE TIPPED DUCKS: two ducks beside a painted hull with their tails straight up and their heads entirely underwater, perfectly calm, their orange feet paddling air as though this were a very ordinary Tuesday

THE MOORING BIRD: a long-legged bird standing on a mooring post at the far side of the canal, small and still, one foot raised, watching the market traffic with the composed expression of a toll collector

THE ROOF FLOCK: a small flock of white birds settled in a long even row along a roof ridge at the far side, tiny in the frame, their reflections trembling in the water below them like dropped stitches
THE STOLEN FRUIT: a small monkey perched on a boat's awning pole, tiny and side-on, holding a round yellow fruit in both hands and eating it with the calm concentration of a practised thief

THE GREEN PARROT: a green parrot tiny at the far side of the picture on a small cage hung on a distant stall, gripping the bars with bright red feet, its head tilted at an angle that suggests it is following a conversation and winning
THE BOW DOG: a small dog standing right at the very tip of a moving boat's bow with its ears blown flat and its nose lifted, reading the whole canal ahead like a page it finds extremely interesting

THE CRATE TURTLE: a small turtle on the rim of a half-sunk wooden crate in the near corner, its shell glazed with water, blinking slowly at the passing hulls with the patience of something that has been here much longer than the market

THE OTTERS: a pair of small river otters at the far side of the canal, one on a mossy step and one in the water beside it, both watching a passing boat with their chins raised and their whiskers catching the light

THE STALL SHADOW FISH: a cloud of tiny fish hanging motionless in the dark water directly under a stall's shadow, so dense and so still they look less like animals and more like something the canal is thinking

THE BUFFALO HORNS: the curved horns and broad dark back of a water buffalo showing just above the far bank, small in the frame, moving at a calm walking pace behind the stalls as though running a perfectly ordinary errand

THE LIFTING HERON: a heron lifting off low across the canal at the far side, small, its wings open wide and its long legs still trailing as it clears the nearest hull by a comfortable margin it clearly calculated in advance

THE SLEEPING DECK CAT: a small cat curled into a perfect circle on the warm planking of a skiff's stern deck, its nose tucked under its own tail, rocking gently with the boat and entirely unmoved by the market's noise

THE SHADOW CARP: a very large carp drifting slowly through a bright patch of reflected lantern light at mid-distance, its deep red and copper scales lit from below for a single moment before it slides back into the green dark

THE WATCHING MONKEY: a small monkey at the far side sitting on a stack of bundled goods at the edge of a moored boat, tiny in the frame, holding its own tail in both hands and watching the water below with an expression of mild scientific interest
